How long does an analysis take in chromosomix, and how much memory does it need, when it is run over a
whole genome on an ordinary laptop? This notebook answers that for 23 analyses on public data: Hi-C maps
from 69 million to 1.08 billion contacts, a yeast Micro-C map down to 50 bp, and ATAC-seq tracks and
sequence over the whole mouse genome. It ends on **[a deep human map, start to
finish](#a-deep-human-map-start-to-finish)**: six analyses one after the other over the 1.08 billion
contacts, by six `chromosomix` commands and by one Python script running the packages they reproduce.

Each analysis is run on the command line and then in the app, in each of three browsers. **On the
command line**, through `chromosomix`, the command-line form of the app's Analysis panel: it runs the
same code the browser runs, and as a process of its own its time and memory are measured by the
operating system — the wall-clock time from start to finish, the CPU time, and the peak memory (the
largest resident set the process reached). **In the app**, as a reader runs it
(`notebooks/scripts/laptop.mjs`), in the three browser engines Playwright drives headless: Chromium,
which Chrome and Edge are built on; Firefox; and WebKit, Safari's engine. In each, the files the command
names are dropped on the landing page, the task opened from the Analysis panel, every flag of the
command set in its form, and **run** pressed. There the time is the app's own, from the job's dispatch
to its result, as its console records it; the CPU time and the memory are the page's, sampled from the
press to the end. WebKit here is Playwright's build of Safari's engine rather than Safari, which cannot
be run headless or driven so; on a Mac it is the nearest a script comes to it.

The block above says which machine this page was rendered on. The page published at
<https://chromosomix.app/laptop/> is rendered by hand, on a laptop, and committed as
`notebooks/laptop.html`; `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml` renders it on a GitHub runner with every
release too, but keeps that render as the run's artifact and never publishes it. To measure your own,
render it from the root of a clone, on a laptop that is plugged in and otherwise idle, with the app and
the command line built from one commit and the three browsers of the Playwright the timings pin
(`notebooks/viewers`) — on Linux, `playwright install --with-deps`, for the system libraries Firefox
and WebKit need. A Chromium already installed can stand in for Playwright's, named in
`LAPTOP_CHROMIUM` or found under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`; Firefox and WebKit are Playwright's own
builds. `LAPTOP_BROWSERS` names the browsers the app is run in, of `chromium,firefox,webkit`, all three
unless it says, and the page is of those it names.

```bash
npm ci && npm run build && npm run build:cli
npm ci --prefix notebooks/viewers && npx --prefix notebooks/viewers playwright install chromium firefox webkit
pip install jupyter pandas matplotlib pyfaidx bioframe==0.8.0 cooler==0.10.4 cooltools==0.7.1 coolpuppy==1.1.0
quarto render notebooks/laptop.qmd
```

The page is one file and carries its table and its stamp inside it, so committing
`notebooks/laptop.html` is all it takes to publish a render: the site's build unpacks the two beside it.

The data (about 16.9 GB) are downloaded once into `notebooks/work/laptop/data/`; files that
`validation.qmd` has already downloaded are linked rather than downloaded again. The analyses take about
20 minutes on the command line and about as long again in Chromium, with a browser started and the files
opened for each; Firefox and WebKit each take their own, which the results give. The deep human map's
six, both sides, took about a quarter of an hour a run on a GitHub runner, most of it `cooltools.dots`. Each result is saved to
`notebooks/work/laptop/timings.tsv` as soon as it is measured, on the command line or in one browser, so
a second render reads the table instead of running everything again, and one with a browser added runs
that browser alone; set `REDO` below to start over.

```{python}
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import platform
import re
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import geometric_mean

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
import pandas as pd
import pyfaidx

from download import download

REDO = False

HERE = Path.cwd().resolve()
REPO = HERE.parent if HERE.name == 'notebooks' else HERE
CLI = REPO / 'dist-cli' / 'chromosomix.mjs'
APP = REPO / 'dist'
DRIVER = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'scripts' / 'laptop.mjs'
WORK = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'work' / 'laptop'
DATA = WORK / 'data'
TIMINGS = WORK / 'timings.tsv'
DATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
#: The browsers the app is run in, as Playwright names them and as the page does: LAPTOP_BROWSERS, else all three.
NAMES = {'chromium': 'Chromium', 'firefox': 'Firefox', 'webkit': 'WebKit'}
BROWSERS = [one.strip() for one in os.environ.get('LAPTOP_BROWSERS', ','.join(NAMES)).split(',') if one.strip()]
if not BROWSERS or set(BROWSERS) - set(NAMES) or len(set(BROWSERS)) < len(BROWSERS):
    raise ValueError(f"LAPTOP_BROWSERS is {os.environ.get('LAPTOP_BROWSERS')!r}: name each browser once, "
                     f"of {', '.join(NAMES)}.")
#: A Chromium to drive: LAPTOP_CHROMIUM, else the one under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, else Playwright's own.
#: Firefox and WebKit are always Playwright's own.
_browsers = os.environ.get('PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH', '')
EXECUTABLES = {'chromium': os.environ.get('LAPTOP_CHROMIUM') or (
    str(Path(_browsers) / 'chromium') if _browsers and (Path(_browsers) / 'chromium').is_file() else None)}

for built, how in ((CLI, 'npm run build:cli'), (APP / 'index.html', 'npm run build')):
    if not built.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{built} is not there: run `{how}` at the repository root.')
VERSION = subprocess.run(['node', str(CLI), '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split('\n')[0]

# One build of one checkout in both places, as the parity holds them: the app names its build in its
# service worker's cache, `chromosomix-<version>-<commit>`; the command line, on `--version`. Two
# builds of two commits would be two programs timed against each other.
_cli = re.fullmatch(r'chromosomix (\S+)(?: \((\w+)\))?', VERSION)
_app = re.search(r'const CACHE = "([^"]*)"', (APP / 'sw.js').read_text()) if (APP / 'sw.js').exists() else None
if _cli is None or _app is None or _app[1] != '-'.join(filter(None, ('chromosomix', *_cli.groups()))):
    raise RuntimeError(f"dist/ is {_app[1] if _app else 'not the site build'} and dist-cli/ is {VERSION}: "
                       'run `npm run build && npm run build:cli` at the repository root, so both are this checkout.')
# Each browser launched once before any is timed, for its version and to know it is there.
VERSIONS = {}
for _browser in BROWSERS:
    _launched = subprocess.run(['node', str(DRIVER), '--version', _browser, *filter(None, [EXECUTABLES.get(_browser)])],
                               capture_output=True, text=True)
    if _launched.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f'No {NAMES[_browser]} to drive: install it with `npx --prefix notebooks/viewers playwright '
                           f'install {_browser}`, or leave it out of LAPTOP_BROWSERS.\n{_launched.stderr[-2000:]}')
    VERSIONS[_browser] = _launched.stdout.strip()
```

Every file is checked against its MD5 when it is downloaded. The mouse sequence is indexed beside itself
(`mm10.fa.fai`) so that it is read by range; the human one is indexed by the last part, which alone
reads it.

```{python}
                                    '319a04a8d7e41d9eb88e2378ea3ea373'),
    '4DNFIIY4QW2D.bw': (f'{FOURDN}/7fb6d419-a8de-4bc8-9c17-f68f814496a2/4DNFIIY4QW2D.bw',
                        '9f8a3a413f54129a689548a93584cdf4'),
    '4DNFITBRHVZE.bw': (f'{FOURDN}/e567a80e-c7d2-41ff-b12d-67047906c076/4DNFITBRHVZE.bw',
                        '99c928ea99ee1a2a7ec7091260f1e4be'),
    'mm10.fa': (f'{IGENOMES}/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/genome.fa', '34d90c586dc92f5c3e8df3ed24530f4f'),
    'mm10.genes.gtf': (f'{IGENOMES}/Annotation/Genes/genes.gtf', '543ec24bb11a4ff0cf5aa4f695320b82'),
    'hg38.fa': ('https://ngi-igenomes.s3.amazonaws.com/igenomes/Homo_sapiens/UCSC/hg38/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/'
                'genome.fa', '9ce261c4aaf4b6092888ef298d190da2'),
}
VALIDATION_DATA = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'work' / 'validation' / 'data'


def md5(path):
    digest = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 22), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def fetch(name, url, expected):
    path = DATA / name
    if path.exists():
        return
    if (VALIDATION_DATA / name).exists():
        path.symlink_to(VALIDATION_DATA / name)
        return
    print('downloading', url)
    part = download(url, path.with_name(name + '.part'))  # asked again when its server fails
    if md5(part) != expected:
        part.unlink()
        raise ValueError(f'{url} did not download as published: its MD5 is not {expected}.')
    part.rename(path)


for name, (url, expected) in FILES.items():
    fetch(name, url, expected)
pyfaidx.Faidx(str(DATA / 'mm10.fa')).close()

pd.DataFrame([{'file': name, 'GB': round((DATA / name).stat().st_size / 1e9, 2)} for name in FILES]) \
    .style.hide(axis='index').format(precision=2)
```

## The analyses

Each analysis is one command, run from `notebooks/work/laptop/` with its output in `out/<name>/`. Two of
them read another's output: the pileup (APA) is over the loops chromosight called, and the overlap is
of the peaks called on the ATAC-seq replicates against the RefSeq transcripts. Parameters are the app's
defaults, except where the validation notebook uses others for the same analysis.

In the app, each command becomes what a reader does to run it (`session` below). A command on a map
opens it as a workspace names it — the file at the command's resolution, balanced, its whole genome on
screen — and the file is dropped on the landing page with the other the command names, a set of loops,
as a track beside it; a command on tracks or sequence alone drops its files alone, a FASTA with its
index. The task is opened from the Analysis panel by the title `chromosomix tasks` gives it, and every
flag of the command is set in its form, the parameter it names: a number typed, a choice chosen, a
switch turned on, a file chosen by its name among those open and the tracks ticked. `--features` and
`--sequence` are the exception: they open the feature sets and the reference a task reads, and the form
chooses the one open for itself, or the two `--a` and `--b` name.

```{python}
#: Every task's title in the Analysis panel, its parameters and their defaults, as `chromosomix tasks`
#: lists them: a parameter listed with none is one the form answers from what is open.
_tasks = subprocess.run(['node', str(CLI), 'tasks'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
TITLES = dict(re.findall(r'^(\w+)\n {4}(\S.*)$', _tasks, re.M))
PARAMETERS, DEFAULTS = {}, {}
for _block in _tasks.split('\n\n'):
    _id = _block.strip().split('\n')[0]
    PARAMETERS[_id] = set(re.findall(r'^ {6}--(\w+)\b', _block, re.M))
    DEFAULTS[_id] = {key: value.strip('"') for key, value in re.findall(r'^ {6}--(\w+) \(default (.*?)\)  ', _block, re.M)}

#: The flags that open what a task reads rather than set its form.
OPENED = {'features', 'sequence'}


def stem(path):
    """A file as the app names it once it is open: its name, up to its first dot."""
    return Path(path).name.split('.')[0]


def beside_the_map(number, path):
    """A file a command reads beside its map, as a workspace names it: a set of loops, on the map."""
    if not path.endswith('.bedpe'):
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: a BEDPE of loops is the one file opened beside a map here.')
    return {'id': f'pairs{number}', 'card': 'overlay', 'kind': 'pairs', 'label': stem(path),
            'source': {'kind': 'local', 'name': Path(path).name}, 'visible': True,
            'placement': {'bottom': True, 'right': False}}


def session(name, args):
    """What the app is handed for one command: the files it names, the workspace that frames its map,
    the task's title and every setting of its form."""
    task, *words = args
    the_map, files, form = None, [], []
    while words:
        word = words.pop(0)
        if not word.startswith('--'):
            the_map = word
            continue
        key = word[2:]
        value = words.pop(0) if words and not words[0].startswith('--') else None
        paths = [] if value is None else [one for one in value.split(',') if one.startswith(('data/', 'out/'))]
        if value is None:
            form.append({'key': key, 'on': True})
        elif not paths:
            form.append({'key': key, 'value': value})
        else:
            files += [one for one in paths if one not in files]
            if key == 'tracks':
                form.append({'key': key, 'ticks': [stem(one) for one in paths]})
            elif key not in OPENED:
                form.append({'key': key, 'option': stem(value)})
    files += [f'{one}.fai' for one in files if one.endswith('.fa')]
    plan = {'name': name, 'task': TITLES[task], 'set': form, 'files': files}
    if the_map is not None:
        path, group = the_map.split('::')
        plan['files'] = [path, *files]
        plan['workspace'] = {'kind': 'chromosomix.workspace', 'version': 1, 'active': 0, 'tabs': [{
            'version': 1, 'state': {'uri': f'{Path(path).name}::{group}', 'view': 'whole', 'balance': True},
            'tracks': [beside_the_map(number, one) for number, one in enumerate(files)]}]}
    return plan
```

Each analysis is run on the command line and then in each browser, one after another, and the first of
them to read a file would find it on disk where the others find it in the system's memory: an 8.3 GB map
read from disk took the run that read it first more than twice as long. So before each run, on the
command line or in a browser, every file the command names is read through once, and every run starts
from files the system holds in memory, as a reader's do once they have opened them.

On the command line, each command runs as a process of its own, and `os.wait4` returns what the system
counted of it: its CPU time, user and system, and its peak resident memory (`ru_maxrss`, which macOS
gives in bytes and Linux in kilobytes).

In the app, each command runs in each browser in turn, a browser of its own, launched for it and closed
after it, so that nothing an earlier run read or drew is in what this one holds. Once the files are open
and the form is set, the page is left until the map is drawn, the app has measured which of its
sequences are circles, and the browser is idle — what the app starts by itself once a map is open is
over before the run — and then **run** is pressed. A page waiting on the disk spends no CPU, and the
measure of the circles reads at a few percent of a core, so neither is told apart from idle by the CPU:
the app's own word that it has drawn a map, and that it has measured its circles, is waited for. Until the console records the run's
end, the browser's processes are sampled five times a second, the same way in the three: their CPU times
and resident sets as the operating system counts them, from `/proc` on Linux and `ps` on macOS. The
page's are the processes that render pages — Chromium's renderers, Firefox's web content processes,
WebKit's web processes — whose threads are its workers, where the app computes and holds what it reads;
its CPU time is what they spent between the press and the end, and its peak memory their largest
resident set — sampled, so a peak shorter than a fifth of a second can be missed, where `ru_maxrss`
cannot miss one. The browser's other processes — the browser itself, which reads the dropped files for
the page, and its GPU, network and storage processes — are counted apart, as `all_cpu_s` and
`all_peak_mb` in the table under the results, the page's included. Each draws as it does headless:
Chromium draws WebGL in software (SwiftShader) and composites the page in software too; Firefox and
WebKit draw as Playwright launches them, Firefox allowed WebGL whatever its blocklist says of the
machine's graphics. A reader's browser has a GPU for all of it. Each run leaves what it was handed, what
it measured and a picture of the page at its end in `notebooks/work/laptop/app/<browser>/<name>/`.

```{python}
def on_the_command_line(name, args):
    """One command: its wall-clock and CPU seconds, and its peak memory in MB."""
    out = WORK / 'out' / name
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as err:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        process = subprocess.Popen(['node', str(CLI), *args, '--out', f'out/{name}', '--quiet'], cwd=WORK,
                                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=err)
        _, status, usage = os.wait4(process.pid, 0)
        wall = time.perf_counter() - start
        if os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status):
            err.seek(0)
            raise RuntimeError(f'chromosomix {" ".join(args)} failed:\n{err.read().decode()[-3000:]}')
    peak = usage.ru_maxrss / (2**20 if sys.platform == 'darwin' else 2**10)
    return {'wall_s': wall, 'cpu_s': usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime, 'peak_mb': peak}


#: What a run in the app measures beside the command line's three: the page before the run, the opening
#: of its files, and every process of the browser.
APP_ONLY = ['rest_mb', 'open_s', 'all_cpu_s', 'all_peak_mb']


def in_the_app(name, args, browser):
    """One command run in the app in one browser: its time, the page's CPU seconds and peak memory in MB,
    all of the browser's, and the line its console wrote — or, where it did not finish, why."""
    folder = WORK / 'app' / browser / name
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    plan = {**session(name, args), 'browser': browser, 'app': str(APP), 'data': str(WORK), 'out': str(folder),
            'executablePath': EXECUTABLES.get(browser)}
    (folder / 'plan.json').write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=1))
    (folder / 'result.json').unlink(missing_ok=True)
    driven = subprocess.run(['node', str(DRIVER), str(folder / 'plan.json'), str(folder / 'result.json')],
                            capture_output=True, text=True)
    if not (folder / 'result.json').exists():
        raise RuntimeError(f'{DRIVER.name} wrote no result for {name} in {NAMES[browser]}:\n{driven.stderr[-3000:]}')
    result = json.loads((folder / 'result.json').read_text())
    ran = result['status'] == 'ok'
    measured = {key: result[key] if ran else math.nan for key in ['wall_s', 'cpu_s', 'peak_mb', *APP_ONLY]}
    return {**measured, 'line': result.get('line', ''), 'error': '' if ran else result.get('error', 'failed')}


#: Where each analysis is run, in order — the command line, then each browser — and what each is: Node's
#: version on the command line, the browser's in the app.
VENUES = ['command line', *(NAMES[one] for one in BROWSERS)]
APPS = VENUES[1:]
PROGRAMS = {'command line': MACHINE['node'], **{NAMES[one]: VERSIONS[one] for one in BROWSERS}}


def kept():
    """What an earlier render of this same build measured, run by run: on the command line in this same
    Node, and in each browser asked for at the version it is now. A run the app did not finish is run
    again."""
    if REDO or not TIMINGS.exists():
        return []
    done = pd.read_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t', dtype={'version': str})
    if not {'venue', 'version', 'error'} <= set(done.columns):
        return []
    done = done.fillna({'line': '', 'error': '', 'version': ''})
    same = (done['chromosomix'] == MACHINE['chromosomix']) & (done['version'] == done['venue'].map(PROGRAMS))
    return done[same & (done['error'] == '') & done['wall_s'].notna()].to_dict('records')


def save(rows):
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t', index=False)


def warm(name, args):
    """Read through every file a command names, so that no run pays alone for reading them from disk."""
    for path in session(name, args)['files']:
        with open(WORK / path, 'rb') as handle:
            while handle.read(1 << 24):
                pass


# Each command on the command line and then in each browser — the pileup's loops and the overlap's peaks
# are the command line's, so every venue reads the same files — and each run saved as soon as it is
# measured, one row each.
rows = kept()
for name, data, analysis, resolution, args in TASKS:
    task = {'name': name, 'data': data, 'analysis': analysis, 'resolution': resolution}
    done = {row['venue'] for row in rows if row['name'] == name}
    for venue, browser in zip(VENUES, [None, *BROWSERS]):
        if venue in done:
            continue
        warm(name, args)
        measured = on_the_command_line(name, args) if browser is None else in_the_app(name, args, browser)
        rows.append({**task, 'venue': venue, 'version': PROGRAMS[venue], **measured,
                     'command': 'chromosomix ' + ' '.join(args), **MACHINE})
        save(rows)

#: Every run, one row each, in the order of TASKS and of VENUES; and each analysis once, with its labels.
ORDER = [task[0] for task in TASKS]
times = pd.DataFrame(rows).fillna({'line': '', 'error': ''})
for column in APP_ONLY:
    times[column] = times[column] if column in times else math.nan
times = times.sort_values(['name', 'venue'], key=lambda column: column.map(
    {'name': ORDER, 'venue': VENUES}[column.name].index)).reset_index(drop=True)
times['added_mb'] = times['peak_mb'] - times['rest_mb']
TASK = times.drop_duplicates('name').set_index('name').loc[ORDER, ['data', 'analysis', 'resolution', 'command']]
FAILED = times[times['error'] != '']


def wide(column, venues=VENUES):
    """One measure of every analysis, a column for each venue."""
    return times.pivot(index='name', columns='venue', values=column).reindex(index=ORDER, columns=venues)
```

```{python}
def duration(seconds):
    if math.isnan(seconds):
        return '—'
    return f'{seconds:.1f} s' if seconds < 60 else f'{seconds / 60:.1f} min'


def megabytes(mb):
    return '—' if math.isnan(mb) else f'{mb:,.0f}'


# A time kept on one line in a cell: `3.7 min` broken after its number reads as two figures.
unbroken = lambda seconds: duration(seconds).replace(' ', '\N{NO-BREAK SPACE}')


def measure(heading, column, shown, added=False):
    """A table of one measure: each analysis, and a column for each venue under the measure's heading —
    and, for the memory, beside the whole peak, what the run added to the page in each browser."""
    table = pd.DataFrame({('', key): TASK[key].values for key in ['data', 'analysis', 'resolution']})
    for venue, values in wide(column).items():
        table[(heading, venue)] = values.map(shown).values
    if added:
        for venue, values in wide('added_mb', APPS).items():
            table[('added by the run (MB)', venue)] = values.map(shown).values
    table.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(table.columns)
    return table.style.hide(axis='index')
```

```{python}
def listing(words):
    """`a`, `a and b`, `a, b and c`."""
    words = [str(word) for word in words]
    return ' and '.join(words) if len(words) < 3 else f"{', '.join(words[:-1])} and {words[-1]}"


def where(venue):
    return 'on the command line' if venue == 'command line' else f'in {venue}'


def extremes(venue):
    """Of one venue's runs: how many took under a minute, the slowest, and the one that held the most —
    none, where none finished."""
    ran = times[(times['venue'] == venue) & times['wall_s'].notna()]
    if ran.empty:
        return 0, None, None
    return int((ran['wall_s'] < 60).sum()), ran.loc[ran['wall_s'].idxmax()], ran.loc[ran['peak_mb'].idxmax()]


def ratios(series, of):
    """A set of ratios, analysis by analysis, in words."""
    if series.empty:
        return 'no analysis finished in both to compare'
    return f'{series.median():.1f} times {of} at the median, from {series.min():.1f} to {series.max():.1f} times'


def on_average(venue):
    """A browser's CPU time and peak memory over the command line's, as geometric means of its analyses."""
    cpu, memory = ((measured[venue] / measured['command line']).dropna() for measured in (CPU, PEAK))
    if cpu.empty:
        return f'{where(venue)}, no analysis finished in both to compare'
    return (f"{where(venue)}, {geometric_mean(cpu):.1f} times the command line's CPU time and "
            f"{geometric_mean(memory):.1f} times its peak memory")


EXTREMES = {venue: extremes(venue) for venue in VENUES}
WALL, CPU, PEAK = wide('wall_s'), wide('cpu_s'), wide('peak_mb')
#: Each browser's time over the command line's, analysis by analysis; and, for each browser after the
#: first, its time and its memory over the first's.
AGAINST_THE_LINE = {venue: (WALL[venue] / WALL['command line']).dropna() for venue in APPS}
FIRST, OTHERS = APPS[0], APPS[1:]
AGAINST_THE_FIRST = {venue: ((WALL[venue] / WALL[FIRST]).dropna(), (PEAK[venue] / PEAK[FIRST]).dropna())
                     for venue in OTHERS}
UNFINISHED = {venue: int((FAILED['venue'] == venue).sum()) for venue in APPS}
```

```{python}
                for venue, (_, slow, _) in EXTREMES.items() if slow is not None]
largest_each = [f"{where(venue)}, {large['peak_mb']:,.0f} MB, for {large['analysis']} ({large['data']})"
                for venue, (_, _, large) in EXTREMES.items() if large is not None]

                for venue, series in AGAINST_THE_LINE.items()]

                 for venue, (wall, peak) in AGAINST_THE_FIRST.items()]

      f"the run (geometric means over the analyses each finished).")

    print(f"- **The browsers against {FIRST}:** {'; '.join(against_first)}.")

    print(f"- **Finished:** {listing(finished)}; the others are listed above the tables.")
else:
    print(f"- **Finished:** every analysis, in {'every browser' if OTHERS else FIRST}.")
```

The command line's CPU time is close to its wall-clock time because it computes on one thread; it can be
slightly higher, as Node collects garbage and compiles on threads of its own. The app computes in its
workers, and its page draws and answers the reader while they do, so its CPU time is theirs and the
page's together. Where a task shares its work — pastis-NB's likelihood, in the two 3D models — the app
shares it with a helper worker for each core the browser reports but its own, seven at most, where the
command line keeps to one thread unless `--threads` asks for more: there the app can take less time
than the command line and more CPU.

```{python}
def asked(line):
    """What a line asks for, flag by flag: each value as written, a file by its name, a switch as true or
    false — and its map, as `map`."""
    out = {}
    words = shlex.split(line)[2:]
    while words:
        word = words.pop(0)
        if not word.startswith('--'):
            path, _, group = word.partition('::')
            out['map'] = [Path(path).name + (f'::{group}' if group else '')]
            continue
        key, _, value = word[2:].partition('=')
        if not value:
            value = words.pop(0) if words and not words[0].startswith('--') else 'true'
        out.setdefault(key, []).extend(Path(one).name if one.startswith(('data/', 'out/')) else one
                                       for one in value.split(','))
    return {key: ','.join(values) for key, values in out.items()}


def alike(a, b):
    """Two values written alike, or two numbers that are one."""
    try:
        return a == b or float(a) == float(b)
    except ValueError:
        return False


def differences(task, command, line):
    """Where the app's line asks for other than the command does: a flag of the command's it does not
    write as written, and one of its own that is not the task's parameter at its default, or one the
    form answers from what is open."""
    ours, theirs = asked(command), asked(line)
    named = set(','.join(theirs.values()).split(','))
    out = []
    for key, value in ours.items():
        if key in OPENED:
            out += [f'does not name {one}' for one in value.split(',') if one not in named]
        elif not alike(value, theirs.get(key)):
            out.append(f"--{key} {theirs.get(key, '(none)')}, for {value}")
    for key, value in theirs.items():
        if key in ours or (key in PARAMETERS[task] and key not in DEFAULTS[task]):
            continue
        if not alike(value, DEFAULTS[task].get(key)):
            out.append(f'adds --{key} {value}')
    return out


#: Every line a browser wrote, held to the command it ran for: where it asks for anything else, what.
DIFFERENT = {(row['name'], row['venue']): differences(row['command'].split()[1], row['command'], row['line'])
             for _, row in LINES.iterrows()}
DIFFERENT = {run: found for run, found in DIFFERENT.items() if found}
```

## A deep human map, start to finish

Each analysis above is one command, timed alone, and by chromosomix alone. This last part times what a
reader runs on a deep map, and against the packages chromosomix reproduces: six analyses, one after the
other, over the human map above — 4DN's in situ Hi-C of IMR-90 (Rao et al. 2014; 4DNFIJTOIGOI, GRCh38,
1.08 billion contacts, an 8.3 GB `.mcool`) — the first five over the whole genome, the last over one
chromosome, each with the settings its section of `{python} R.link('validation')` holds it to:

1. **Loop calling** at 10 kb: HiCCUPS as `cooltools.dots` computes it, at its Python API's defaults,
   over the expected with the first two diagonals left out (§ 19);
2. **Diamond insulation** at 10 kb, a window of 10 bins, 100 kb, and its boundaries (§ 1);
3. **Compartments** at 250 kb: three cis eigenvectors, signed by each bin's GC content, which is
   worked out once beforehand — `bioframe.frac_gc` over hg38 as Illumina iGenomes distributes UCSC's —
   and given to both (§ 3);
4. **APA over every loop** step 1 called: five bins either side of each, ±50 kb, of balanced counts
   with no expected — the pileup raw — the first two diagonals left out and no loop for being near
   the diagonal (§ 11, *raw, every loop*);
5. **P(s)** at 10 kb: the mean balanced contact at each separation, over every chromosome, every
   diagonal kept, cooltools' `expected_cis` unsmoothed and pooled over the bands chromosomix writes
   (§ 4) — its own, not the one step 1 read, which left two diagonals out;
6. **Virtual 4C** at 10 kb, in cis: what one bin, the one holding *MYC*'s transcription start on
   chr8, touches on its own chromosome, balanced (§ 10, which reads the whole genome).
   `cooltools.virtual4c` has no cis of its own, so the script hands it a map over the viewpoint's
   chromosome alone (its `map_functor`), on which it runs the same profile it runs on each chromosome
   of the genome — through the function undecorated, since cooltools 0.7.1's decorator passes a
   `map_functor` it is given on twice.

**chromosomix** runs them as a shell script would: six commands, one after the other, the pileup
reading the loops the first wrote. **The reference** is one Python script,
`notebooks/scripts/cooltools_pipeline.py`, which runs the six through cooltools and coolpuppy in one
process, its pileup over the loops `cooltools.dots` called. Neither side's pileup reads an expected,
so neither is spared one the other pays for, and each side's P(s) is a step of its own, as the loop
calling's expected is inside its own; chromosomix's compartments draw the saddle too, at the task's
default, which `cooltools.eigs_cis` does not. `chromosomix` computes on one thread; the script gives
every call that takes them `P_THREADS` processes — one a core, at most four, as the validation gives
its references — but for the 4C, one chromosome in one process. This part alone needs the reference
packages, at the versions `notebooks/requirements.txt` pins: cooler, cooltools, coolpuppy and bioframe.

**Start-up, each step and the whole.** A command's start-up is the program loaded and nothing done,
`chromosomix --version`, timed as a command of its own, which each of the six pays again before its
task: each step is its command, from its launch to its exit, its own start-up and the opening of the
map included, and the whole is the six. The script's start-up runs from its launch to the end of its
imports — Python itself, cooler, cooltools and coolpuppy — and each step from the end of the one before
it to its own, as the script writes them down; the whole is the process, from its launch to its exit.
The CPU time of a command, and of the script's whole, is `os.wait4`'s, as above; a step of the
script's, what its process and every child it had waited for had used at either end — cooltools' and
coolpuppy's pools are waited for when each call returns. The memory is weighed every `EVERY` seconds:
the process and every process under it, together — their proportional set sizes where the system
gives them, as Linux does, a page two of them share counted half in each; elsewhere, as on a Mac,
their resident sets as `ps` lists them, a page shared counted in each, so that a pool of forked workers
reads as more than it holds. A command's peak, and the script's whole, is never less than the largest
resident set any one of its processes reached, which a weighing can miss; a step of the script's, the
most its processes held together in the weighings taken between its ends.

**One run of each side, unless `PIPELINE_RUNS` says otherwise.** Each side reads the map from the disk,
the page cache emptied before it where the machine lets the benchmark do so; where it does not, as on a
Mac, the map is read through once before each side instead, so that both find it in memory (the
`page_cache` column). Over several runs the two take turns to go first. Every step of every run, its
start-up and the whole among them, is one line of **`notebooks/work/laptop/pipeline.tsv`**, with when
in its side's run it began and ended; and every weighing of each side's processes, with when it was
taken and the step it fell in, is one line of **`pipeline-memory.tsv`** beside it, which the figure at
the end draws against the time. The page carries both, as it carries the table above. A second render
reads them back (`REDO_PIPELINE`), unless the build, the script or the number of runs has changed.

```{python}
from importlib.metadata import version as installed_version
import threading

def show(frame, precision=2, **formats):
    """A table without row numbers: the columns named in `formats` their way, the others to `precision`."""
    return frame.style.hide(axis='index').format(formats or None, precision=precision)


def measures(values):
    """Named numbers as a two-column table."""
    return pd.DataFrame(list(values.items()), columns=['measure', 'value']).style.hide(axis='index')


# The GC content of each 250-kb bin of the map, once: a table for cooltools, a bedGraph for chromosomix.
```

```{python}
#: How often, in seconds, a side's processes are weighed while it runs.
EVERY = 0.25
#: Whether the system gives each process's proportional set size, as Linux does: where it does not, as a
#: Mac does not, a process weighs its resident set.
PSS = Path('/proc/self/smaps_rollup').exists()


def pss_kb(pid):
    """A process's proportional set size, in kB: its resident pages, one it shares with others counted as its
    share of it, so that a pool of forked workers is not counted again in each."""
    try:
        with open(f'/proc/{pid}/smaps_rollup') as handle:
            return next(int(line.split()[1]) for line in handle if line.startswith('Pss:'))
    except (OSError, StopIteration):
        return 0


def held_kb(pid):
    """What `pid` and every process under it hold together, in kB, found by their parents as `ps` lists them,
    on Linux and on a Mac alike: their proportional set sizes where the system gives them, and their resident
    sets elsewhere."""
    listed = subprocess.run(['ps', '-A', '-o', 'pid=,ppid=,rss='], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
    children, rss = {}, {}
    for at in range(0, len(listed) - 2, 3):
        one, parent, kb = (int(value) for value in listed[at:at + 3])
        children.setdefault(parent, []).append(one)
        rss[one] = kb
    found, todo = [], [pid]
    while todo:
        one = todo.pop()
        found.append(one)
        todo += children.get(one, [])
    return sum(pss_kb(one) if PSS else rss.get(one, 0) for one in found)


def weigh(pid, done, peak, samples=None):
    """Every EVERY seconds until `done`, the processes under `pid` weighed together, the most into `peak[0]`,
    and each weighing into `samples`, with when it was taken, where there is a list to keep them."""
    while True:
        held = held_kb(pid)
        peak[0] = max(peak[0], held)
        if samples is not None:
            samples.append((time.time(), held))
        if done.wait(EVERY):
            return


def timed(argv, cwd, samples=None):
    """One run, from `cwd`: CPU seconds of the process and every process it started and waited for, wall
    seconds, and the most memory they held together, in MB; every weighing of them into `samples`, if it is
    a list."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as err:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        process = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=err)
        done, peak = threading.Event(), [0]
        weigher = threading.Thread(target=weigh, args=(process.pid, done, peak, samples), daemon=True)
        weigher.start()
        _, status, usage = os.wait4(process.pid, 0)
        wall = time.perf_counter() - start
        done.set()
        weigher.join()
        if os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status):
            err.seek(0)
            raise RuntimeError(f'{shlex.join(argv)}\n{err.read().decode(errors="replace")[-3000:]}')
    # ru_maxrss, the largest resident set any one of the processes reached, which a weighing can miss: in
    # kilobytes on Linux and in bytes on a Mac.
    largest = usage.ru_maxrss / (2**20 if sys.platform == 'darwin' else 2**10)
    return {'cpu_s': usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime, 'wall_s': wall, 'peak_mb': max(peak[0] / 1024, largest)}
```

```{python}
PIPELINE_SCRIPT = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'scripts' / 'cooltools_pipeline.py'
#: The six steps, in their order: what the tables call each, and what it reads.
PIPELINE_STEPS = {'loops': ('Loop calling', '10 kb'), 'insulation': ('Diamond insulation', '10 kb, 10 bins'),
                  'compartments': ('Compartments', '250 kb, GC-phased'),
                  'apa': ('APA over every loop', '10 kb, ±5 bins, raw'),
                  'ps': ('P(s)', '10 kb, every diagonal'), 'fourc': ('Virtual 4C', '10 kb, one bin, cis')}
#: The 4C's viewpoint: the 10-kb bin holding MYC's transcription start, chr8:127,735,434 in GRCh38 (+ strand), as
#: cooltools reads a region (0-based, half-open) and as chromosomix does (1-based, inclusive).
FOURC_BIN = ('chr8', 127_730_000, 127_740_000)
FOURC_COOLTOOLS = f'{FOURC_BIN[0]}:{FOURC_BIN[1]}-{FOURC_BIN[2]}'
FOURC_ANCHOR = f'{FOURC_BIN[0]}:{FOURC_BIN[1] + 1:,}-{FOURC_BIN[2]:,}'
#: And the start-up before them, and the whole of them.
PIPELINE_TASKS = {'start-up': ('Start-up', ''), **PIPELINE_STEPS, 'total': ('Total', '')}


def in_a_sentence(name):
    """A step's name inside a sentence: its first letter lowered, unless what follows it is not a small letter
    (APA, P(s))."""
    return name[0].lower() + name[1:] if name[1:2].islower() else name

#: The script's processes: one a core, at most four, as validation.qmd's THREADS gives its references.
P_THREADS = min(4, os.cpu_count() or 1)
P_SIDES = {'chromosomix': 'chromosomix',
           'reference': ', '.join(f'{name} {installed_version(name)}' for name in ('cooltools', 'coolpuppy', 'cooler'))}
P_SCRIPT = hashlib.sha256(PIPELINE_SCRIPT.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:10]
P_OUT = {side: PWORK / 'runs' / side for side in P_SIDES}


def p_rel(path):
    return os.path.relpath(path, PWORK)


def p_map(bp):
    return f'{p_rel(IMR90)}::/resolutions/{bp}'


def app_argv(step, out):
    """chromosomix's command for one step, writing into `out`: the pileup reads the loops the first wrote there."""
    program = ['node', p_rel(CLI)]
    if step == 'start-up':
        return [*program, '--version']
    argv = {'loops': ['loops', p_map(10_000)],
            'insulation': ['insulation', p_map(10_000), '--window', '10'],
            'compartments': ['compartments', p_map(250_000), '--components', '3', '--phaseTrack', p_rel(GC_BEDGRAPH)],
            'ps': ['expected', p_map(10_000), '--quantity', 'expected', '--scope', 'file'],
            'fourc': ['fourc', p_map(10_000), '--anchor', FOURC_ANCHOR]}
    if step == 'apa':
        argv['apa'] = ['apa', p_map(10_000), '--pairs', p_rel(one_file(out / 'loops', '*.loops-calls.bedpe')),
                       '--mode', 'fixed', '--window', '5', '--minDiag', '2', '--minDist', '0', '--norm', 'none']
    return [*program, *argv[step], '--out', p_rel(out / step)]


def script_argv(out):
    """The script's one command, writing beside `out/cooltools` and its marks to `out/marks.json`."""
    return [sys.executable, p_rel(PIPELINE_SCRIPT), p_rel(IMR90), p_rel(GC_TSV), FOURC_COOLTOOLS,
            p_rel(out / 'cooltools'), str(P_THREADS), p_rel(out / 'marks.json')]


def one_file(folder, pattern):
    hits = sorted(Path(folder).glob(pattern))
    if len(hits) != 1:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{len(hits)} files match {pattern} in {folder}')
    return hits[0]


def typed_line(argv):
    """A command as a reader would type it."""
    if argv[:2] == ['node', p_rel(CLI)]:
        argv = ['chromosomix', *argv[2:]]
    return shlex.join(['python' if a == sys.executable else a for a in argv])


def settle():
    """Before each side: the page cache emptied where the machine lets the benchmark do so, so that each reads
    the map from the disk, as at a first opening; elsewhere the map read through once, so that each finds it
    in memory. Which of the two, as the table says it."""
    subprocess.run(['sync'])
    try:
        if subprocess.run(['sudo', '-n', 'sh', '-c', 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'],
                          capture_output=True).returncode == 0:
            return 'dropped'
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    with open(IMR90, 'rb') as handle:
        while handle.read(1 << 24):
            pass
    return 'read through'


#: The columns of pipeline.tsv, in order: the side and the step, the run, what it cost, when in the side's
#: run it began and ended (`from_s`, `to_s`, seconds since the side's first launch), where.
PIPELINE_COLUMNS = ['side', 'tool', 'version', 'step', 'task', 'reads', 'run', 'went_first', 'page_cache',
                    'threads', 'cpu_s', 'wall_s', 'peak_mb', 'from_s', 'to_s', 'started', *MACHINE, 'python',
                    'script', 'map', 'command_line']
#: Every weighing of a side's processes, by the step it fell in: seconds since the side's first launch, and
#: the memory they held together, in MB. What the figure draws against the time.
PIPELINE_TRACE = WORK / 'pipeline-memory.tsv'
TRACE_COLUMNS = ['side', 'tool', 'run', 'step', 'seconds', 'mb']


def p_row(side, step, run, first, cache, cost, line, started, span=(np.nan, np.nan)):
    return {'side': side, 'tool': 'chromosomix' if side == 'chromosomix' else 'cooltools, coolpuppy',
            'version': MACHINE['chromosomix'] if side == 'chromosomix' else P_SIDES[side], 'step': step,
            'task': PIPELINE_TASKS[step][0], 'reads': PIPELINE_TASKS[step][1], 'run': run,
            'went_first': first == side, 'page_cache': cache,
            'threads': 1 if side == 'chromosomix' else P_THREADS, 'cpu_s': cost['cpu_s'], 'wall_s': cost['wall_s'],
            'peak_mb': cost['peak_mb'], 'from_s': span[0], 'to_s': span[1], 'started': started, **MACHINE,
            'python': platform.python_version(), 'script': P_SCRIPT, 'map': IMR90.name, 'command_line': line}


def p_trace(side, run, step, at, kb):
    return {'side': side, 'tool': 'chromosomix' if side == 'chromosomix' else 'cooltools, coolpuppy', 'run': run,
            'step': step, 'seconds': at, 'mb': kb / 1024}


def app_side(run, first):
    """chromosomix's side of one run: its start-up, its six commands and their whole, and every weighing of the
    six, its time counted from the launch of the first. The start-up, `--version`, is timed before them and
    is no part of that time: each command pays its own, inside its step."""
    out = P_OUT['chromosomix']
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    cache, rows, trace, first_launch = settle(), [], [], None
    for step in ['start-up', *PIPELINE_STEPS]:
        argv = app_argv(step, out)
        started = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
        samples = None if step == 'start-up' else []
        launched = time.time()
        cost = timed(argv, PWORK, samples)
        span = (np.nan, np.nan)
        if step != 'start-up':
            first_launch = launched if first_launch is None else first_launch
            span = (launched - first_launch, launched + cost['wall_s'] - first_launch)
            trace += [p_trace('chromosomix', run, step, at - first_launch, kb) for at, kb in samples]
        rows.append(p_row('chromosomix', step, run, first, cache, cost, typed_line(argv), started, span))
    steps = rows[1:]
    whole = {'cpu_s': sum(r['cpu_s'] for r in steps), 'wall_s': sum(r['wall_s'] for r in steps),
             'peak_mb': max(r['peak_mb'] for r in steps)}
    rows.append(p_row('chromosomix', 'total', run, first, cache, whole,
                      '; '.join(r['command_line'] for r in steps), steps[0]['started'], (0.0, steps[-1]['to_s'])))
    return rows, trace


def script_side(run, first):
    """The script's side of one run: its start-up and six steps as it marked them, and its whole, and every
    weighing of its processes, its time counted from the script's launch."""
    out = P_OUT['reference']
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    cache, samples = settle(), []
    argv = script_argv(out)
    started = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
    launched = time.time()
    whole = timed(argv, PWORK, samples)
    marks = {mark['step']: mark for mark in json.loads((out / 'marks.json').read_text())['marks']}
    rows, trace, before = [], [], {'time': launched, 'cpu_s': 0.0}
    ends = [('start-up', marks['imported']), *((step, marks[step]) for step in PIPELINE_STEPS)]
    for step, mark in ends:
        held = [kb for at, kb in samples if before['time'] <= at <= mark['time']]
        cost = {'cpu_s': mark['cpu_s'] - before['cpu_s'], 'wall_s': mark['time'] - before['time'],
                'peak_mb': max(held) / 1024 if held else np.nan}
        rows.append(p_row('reference', step, run, first, cache, cost, typed_line(argv), started,
                          (before['time'] - launched, mark['time'] - launched)))
        before = mark
    rows.append(p_row('reference', 'total', run, first, cache, whole, typed_line(argv), started, (0.0, whole['wall_s'])))
    # A weighing in the step whose end is the first after it; one after the last mark, as the process exits, in
    # the last step.
    for at, kb in samples:
        step = next((step for step, mark in ends if at <= mark['time']), ends[-1][0])
        trace.append(p_trace('reference', run, step, at - launched, kb))
    return rows, trace


def pipeline():
    rows, trace = [], []
    PIPELINE_TABLE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for run in range(1, PIPELINE_RUNS + 1):
        # chromosomix first on odd runs, the script on even ones.
        order = ['chromosomix', 'reference'] if run % 2 == 1 else ['reference', 'chromosomix']
        for side in order:
            got, weighed = app_side(run, order[0]) if side == 'chromosomix' else script_side(run, order[0])
            rows += got
            trace += weighed
        # Written after every run, so a long benchmark that is stopped keeps the runs it finished.
        pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=PIPELINE_COLUMNS).to_csv(PIPELINE_TABLE, sep='\t', index=False)
        pd.DataFrame(trace, columns=TRACE_COLUMNS).to_csv(PIPELINE_TRACE, sep='\t', index=False, float_format='%.6g')


def pipeline_current():
    """Whether pipeline.tsv holds every step of PIPELINE_RUNS runs, by this chromosomix and this script, and
    pipeline-memory.tsv their weighings."""
    if REDO_PIPELINE or not PIPELINE_TABLE.exists() or not PIPELINE_TRACE.exists():
        return False
    held = pd.read_csv(PIPELINE_TABLE, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False)
    return (list(held.columns) == PIPELINE_COLUMNS and set(held['run']) == set(range(1, PIPELINE_RUNS + 1))
            and len(held) == PIPELINE_RUNS * 2 * len(PIPELINE_TASKS)
            and set(held['chromosomix']) == {MACHINE['chromosomix']} and set(held['script']) == {P_SCRIPT}
            and all(P_OUT[side].exists() for side in P_SIDES))


if not pipeline_current():
    pipeline()
steps = pd.read_csv(PIPELINE_TABLE, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False, na_values=[''])
weighed = pd.read_csv(PIPELINE_TRACE, sep='\t')
for side, rows in steps.groupby('side', sort=False):
    print(f'# {rows["tool"].iloc[0]}')
    lines = rows.loc[(rows['run'] == 1) & ~rows['step'].isin(['total']), 'command_line']
    print('\n'.join(f'$ {line}' for line in dict.fromkeys(lines)), end='\n\n')
measures({'runs': PIPELINE_RUNS, 'lines in the table': len(steps),
          'measured': f"{steps['started'].min()} to {steps['started'].max()}",
          'page cache before each side': ', '.join(sorted(set(steps['page_cache']))),
          'reference': P_SIDES['reference'], 'table': os.path.relpath(PIPELINE_TABLE, REPO),
          'weighings': f"{len(weighed):,}, every {EVERY} s, to {os.path.relpath(PIPELINE_TRACE, REPO)}"})
```

```{python}

P_SIDE_NAMES = {'chromosomix': 'chromosomix', 'reference': 'cooltools, coolpuppy'}
p_mean = (steps.groupby(['step', 'side'], sort=False)
          .agg(cpu=('cpu_s', 'mean'), wall=('wall_s', 'mean'), peak=('peak_mb', 'max')).reset_index())
p_table = p_mean.pivot(index='step', columns='side', values=['cpu', 'wall', 'peak']).reindex(list(PIPELINE_TASKS))
p_shown = pd.DataFrame({'step': [PIPELINE_TASKS[s][0] for s in p_table.index],

for measure, unit in (('cpu', 'CPU s'), ('wall', 'wall s'), ('peak', 'peak MB')):

        p_shown[f'{P_SIDE_NAMES[side]}, {unit}'] = p_table[(measure, side)].to_numpy()
```

Both sides did the same work: what each wrote in the last run, step by step, against the other's.

```{python}
APP_P, REF_P = P_OUT['chromosomix'], P_OUT['reference']


def app_table(folder, pattern):
    return pd.read_csv(one_file(folder, pattern), sep='\t', comment='#')


p_agree = []
# Loop calling: the same bin pairs.
_app_dots = app_table(APP_P / 'loops', '*.loops-table.tsv')
_ref_dots = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-loops.tsv', sep='\t').rename(columns={'chrom1': 'sequence'})
_dots = _app_dots.merge(_ref_dots, on=['sequence', 'start1', 'start2'], how='outer', indicator=True)
p_agree.append({'step': 'Loop calling', 'chromosomix': f'{len(_app_dots):,} loops',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{len(_ref_dots):,} loops',
                'agreement': f"{int((_dots['_merge'] == 'both').sum()):,} at the same bin pair, "
                             f"{int((_dots['_merge'] != 'both').sum()):,} in one only"})
# Insulation: every bin both score, and the boundaries.
_app_ins = app_table(APP_P / 'insulation', '*.insulation-w10.tsv')['value'].to_numpy(float)
_ref_table = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-insulation.tsv', sep='\t')
_ref_ins = _ref_table['log2_insulation_score_100000'].to_numpy(float)
_both = np.isfinite(_app_ins) & np.isfinite(_ref_ins)
_app_b = app_table(APP_P / 'insulation', '*.insulation-boundaries.tsv')
_ref_b = _ref_table.loc[_ref_table['is_boundary_100000'].astype(bool), ['chrom', 'start']]
_same_b = len(_app_b[['chrom', 'start']].merge(_ref_b, on=['chrom', 'start']))
p_agree.append({'step': 'Diamond insulation', 'chromosomix': f'{len(_app_b):,} boundaries',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{len(_ref_b):,} boundaries',
                'agreement': f'{_same_b:,} boundaries at the same bin; over {_both.sum():,} bins, the score '
                             f'within {np.abs(_app_ins[_both] - _ref_ins[_both]).max():.1e}'})
# Compartments: E1, chromosome by chromosome, chrY left out as § 3 leaves it out.
_app_e1 = app_table(APP_P / 'compartments', '*.compartment-e1.tsv')['value'].to_numpy(float)
_ref_vec = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-eigenvectors.tsv', sep='\t')
_rs = {}
for _chrom in _ref_vec['chrom'].unique():
    _s = (_ref_vec['chrom'] == _chrom).to_numpy()
    _ok = _s & np.isfinite(_app_e1) & np.isfinite(_ref_vec['E1'].to_numpy(float))
    if _chrom != 'chrY' and _ok.sum() > 2:
        _rs[_chrom] = np.corrcoef(_app_e1[_ok], _ref_vec['E1'].to_numpy(float)[_ok])[0, 1]
_low = min(_rs, key=_rs.get)
p_agree.append({'step': 'Compartments', 'chromosomix': 'E1, E2, E3', 'cooltools, coolpuppy': 'E1, E2, E3',
                'agreement': f'E1 at 1 − r ≤ {max(1 - _rs[_low], 1e-16):.0e} (Pearson) on each of {len(_rs)} '
                             f'chromosomes, {_low} the furthest'})
# The pileup: cell for cell.
_app_apa = app_table(APP_P / 'apa', '*.apa-0.tsv')
_app_apa = _app_apa.set_index(_app_apa.columns[0]).to_numpy(float)
_ref_apa = np.loadtxt(REF_P / 'cooltools-apa.tsv', delimiter='\t')
_cells = np.isfinite(_app_apa) & np.isfinite(_ref_apa)
_rel = np.abs(_app_apa - _ref_apa)[_cells] / np.maximum(np.abs(_ref_apa[_cells]), 1e-300)
p_agree.append({'step': 'APA over every loop', 'chromosomix': f'{_app_apa.shape[0]} × {_app_apa.shape[1]}',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{_ref_apa.shape[0]} × {_ref_apa.shape[1]}',
                'agreement': f'{_cells.sum()} cells, within {_rel.max():.1e} of each other, relative; '
                             f'{int((np.isfinite(_app_apa) != np.isfinite(_ref_apa)).sum())} empty in one only'})
# P(s): cooltools' diagonals, summed over the chromosomes, pooled over the bands chromosomix wrote, as § 4 pools them.
from ps_bands import bands, kept_from

_ps_file = one_file(APP_P / 'ps', '*.expected.ps.tsv')
_app_ps = app_table(APP_P / 'ps', '*.expected.ps.tsv')
_cvd = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-ps.tsv', sep='\t')
_cvd['balanced.sum'] = _cvd['balanced.sum'].fillna(0)
_diagonals = _cvd.groupby('dist')[['n_valid', 'balanced.sum']].sum()
_n = _diagonals['n_valid'].reindex(range(int(_diagonals.index.max()) + 1), fill_value=0).to_numpy(float)
_sum = _diagonals['balanced.sum'].reindex(range(len(_n)), fill_value=0).to_numpy(float)
_x, _y = _app_ps.iloc[:, 0].to_numpy(float), _app_ps.iloc[:, 1].to_numpy(float)
_pooled = np.array([_sum[a:b].sum() / _n[a:b].sum() for a, b in bands(_n, _x, _c10.binsize, kept_from(_ps_file))])
p_agree.append({'step': 'P(s)', 'chromosomix': f'{len(_x)} points', 'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{len(_n):,} diagonals',
                'agreement': f'each point within {np.abs(_y / _pooled - 1).max():.1e} of the diagonals it pools, '
                             f'relative'})
# Virtual 4C: bin by bin. cooltools reports a bin the viewpoint has a stored contact with; chromosomix every bin of the
# viewpoint's chromosome, 0 where the map stores none.
_app_4c = app_table(APP_P / 'fourc', '*.fourc-*.tsv')['value'].to_numpy(float)
_ref_4c = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-fourc.tsv', sep='\t')['balanced'].to_numpy(float)
_kept = np.isfinite(_c10.bins()['weight'][:].to_numpy(float))
_both = np.isfinite(_app_4c) & np.isfinite(_ref_4c)
_app_only = np.isfinite(_app_4c) & ~np.isfinite(_ref_4c)
_at = _c10.offset(FOURC_COOLTOOLS)
_rel = np.abs(_app_4c[_both] - _ref_4c[_both]) / np.abs(_ref_4c[_both])
_unread = _app_only & (_app_4c == 0) & _kept
_dropped = _app_only & (_app_4c == 0) & ~_kept
_else = _app_only & ~_unread & ~_dropped
_else[_at] = False
p_agree.append({'step': 'Virtual 4C', 'chromosomix': f'{np.isfinite(_app_4c).sum():,} bins',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{np.isfinite(_ref_4c).sum():,} bins',
                'agreement': f'{_both.sum():,} bins both report, within {_rel.max():.1e} of each other, relative; '
                             f'only in chromosomix, {_unread.sum():,} at 0 where the map stores no contact with the '
                             f'viewpoint, {_dropped.sum():,} at 0 where balancing dropped the bin, the viewpoint'
                             f'{"" if bool(_app_only[_at]) else " (not written)"} and {_else.sum():,} besides; '
                             f'{int((np.isfinite(_ref_4c) & ~np.isfinite(_app_4c)).sum()):,} only in cooltools'})
show(pd.DataFrame(p_agree))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pipeline
#| fig-cap: "The six analyses over the IMR-90 map, one after the other, against the wall clock: the memory each side's processes held together, weighed every quarter of a second, the first run's, each phase shaded behind it and its peak marked. chromosomix is its six commands, back to back, each paying its own start-up inside its phase (`chromosomix --version`, a quarter of a second); the script's start-up, Python and its imports, is paid once, before loop calling."
def minutes(seconds):
    return f'{seconds / 60:.1f} min' if seconds >= 90 else f'{seconds:.0f} s'


#: Each phase's shade, as the R figure shades them (notebooks/scripts/timing.plot.R).
PHASE_COLOURS = {'start-up': '#d9d9d9', 'loops': '#cfe3c1', 'insulation': '#f5e2ad', 'compartments': '#dcd2ec',
                 'apa': '#c6e2ea', 'ps': '#f4cfc7', 'fourc': '#e4d6c3'}
P_SIDE_LABELS = {'chromosomix': 'chromosomix, 1 thread',
                 'reference': f'cooltools and coolpuppy, {P_THREADS} processes'}
first_run = steps[steps['run'] == 1]
traced_run = weighed[weighed['run'] == 1]
ENDS = {side: first_run.loc[(first_run['side'] == side) & (first_run['step'] == 'total'), 'to_s'].iloc[0] / 60
        for side in P_SIDES}
TOP = traced_run['mb'].max() / 1024 * 1.25
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(P_SIDES), 1, figsize=(10, 4.8), sharex=True, sharey=True, layout='constrained')
for ax, side in zip(axes, P_SIDES):
    colour = APP_COLOUR if side == 'chromosomix' else REF
    phases = first_run[(first_run['side'] == side) & first_run['step'].isin(PHASE_COLOURS)].dropna(subset=['from_s'])
    for one in phases.itertuples():
        ax.axvspan(one.from_s / 60, one.to_s / 60, color=PHASE_COLOURS[one.step], alpha=0.6, lw=0, zorder=0)
    points = traced_run[traced_run['side'] == side].sort_values('seconds')
    x, gb = points['seconds'].to_numpy() / 60, points['mb'].to_numpy() / 1024
    ax.fill_between(x, gb, color=colour, alpha=0.3, lw=0, zorder=2)
    ax.plot(x, gb, color=colour, lw=1, zorder=3)
    # Where the weighings peak, and the peak as the table gives it: never less than the largest resident set
    # any one process reached, which a weighing can miss.
    peak = points.loc[points['mb'].idxmax()]
    most = first_run.loc[(first_run['side'] == side) & (first_run['step'] == 'total'), 'peak_mb'].iloc[0]
    name = PIPELINE_TASKS[peak['step']][0]
    ax.scatter([peak['seconds'] / 60], [peak['mb'] / 1024], s=18, color=colour, zorder=4)
    ax.annotate(f"peak {most / 1024:.1f} GB, {in_a_sentence(name)}",
                (peak['seconds'] / 60, peak['mb'] / 1024), xytext=(-6, 4), textcoords='offset points', fontsize=8,
                ha='right')  # over its own phase, not across the line where the side finished
    ax.axvline(ENDS[side], color=INK2, lw=0.8, ls=(0, (3, 2)), zorder=4)
    ax.annotate(f'done, {minutes(ENDS[side] * 60)}', (ENDS[side], TOP * 0.92), xytext=(4, 0),
                textcoords='offset points', fontsize=8, va='top')
    ax.set_title(P_SIDE_LABELS[side], fontsize=9)
    ax.set(ylabel='memory (GB)', ylim=(0, TOP), xlim=(0, max(ENDS.values()) * 1.12))
    ax.grid(False)
axes[-1].set_xlabel('wall-clock time (min)')
handles = [plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, color=c, alpha=0.6) for c in PHASE_COLOURS.values()]
fig.legend(handles, [PIPELINE_TASKS[step][0] for step in PHASE_COLOURS], loc='outside upper right',
           ncols=4, fontsize=8)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
def p_value(step, side, column):
    return float(steps.loc[(steps['step'] == step) & (steps['side'] == side), column].mean())


P_TEXT = {'app': minutes(p_value('total', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s')),
          'ref': minutes(p_value('total', 'reference', 'wall_s')),
          'wall': f"{p_value('total', 'reference', 'wall_s') / p_value('total', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.1f}",
          'cpu': f"{p_value('total', 'reference', 'cpu_s') / p_value('total', 'chromosomix', 'cpu_s'):.1f}",
          'app_peak': f"{steps.loc[steps['side'] == 'chromosomix', 'peak_mb'].max() / 1024:.1f} GB",
          'ref_peak': f"{steps.loc[steps['side'] == 'reference', 'peak_mb'].max() / 1024:.1f} GB",
          'app_start': f"{p_value('start-up', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.2f} s",
          'ref_start': f"{p_value('start-up', 'reference', 'wall_s'):.1f} s",
          'loops': f"{p_value('loops', 'reference', 'wall_s') / p_value('loops', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.1f}"}


def against(step):
    """A step of chromosomix's against the script's: × on the wall clock and × in CPU time, above 1 faster."""
    name = PIPELINE_TASKS[step][0]
    return (f"{in_a_sentence(name)}, "
            f"{p_value(step, 'reference', 'wall_s') / p_value(step, 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.1f}× on the wall clock "
            f"and {p_value(step, 'reference', 'cpu_s') / p_value(step, 'chromosomix', 'cpu_s'):.1f}× in CPU time")


P_SLOWER = [step for step in PIPELINE_STEPS if p_value(step, 'chromosomix', 'wall_s') > p_value(step, 'reference', 'wall_s')]
P_TEXT['slower'] = ('In none of the six is chromosomix slower on the wall clock.' if not P_SLOWER else
                    'On one thread against the script\'s processes, chromosomix is slower on the wall clock at '
                    + '; '.join(against(step) for step in P_SLOWER) + '.')
```

Over the IMR-90 map, the six analyses take **`{python} P_TEXT['app']`** in `chromosomix` and
**`{python} P_TEXT['ref']`** in the Python script: `{python} P_TEXT['wall']` times less wall-clock time
on one thread against the script's `{python} str(P_THREADS)` processes, and `{python} P_TEXT['cpu']` times less CPU
time; at most `{python} P_TEXT['app_peak']` of memory against `{python} P_TEXT['ref_peak']`. Loop
calling is most of either side, and `{python} P_TEXT['loops']` times faster on the wall clock in
`chromosomix`. `{python} P_TEXT['slower']` Starting takes `chromosomix` `{python} P_TEXT['app_start']`
a command, six times, and the script `{python} P_TEXT['ref_start']`, once.
